newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH WINGS ENJOY FLYING EUROPEAN START.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRENCH WINGS ENJOY FLYING EUROPEAN START.

text.p: Flying French wingers Benjamin Lhande and Sebastien Carrat stole the individual honours on the first weekend of European Cup rugby action, running in four tries apiece against British opposition on Saturday.
Lhande was the principal beneficiary as Pau scored 13 tries to rout Scottish Borders 85-28 in pool B in a match which remarkably saw only one penalty awarded.

New Zealander Scott Keith and David Aucagne also collected two tries apiece with Aucagne kicking eight conversions as Borders, who included 11 members of current Scottish league leaders Melrose, struggled badly for possession up front.

Brive encountered greater resistance from Welsh champions Neath in pool C, but a try and three penalties from French international Sebastien Viars, playing at full-back, plus Carrat's quartet took them well clear.
They strung together some fine moves and all their tries were the result of the ball being spun along the line.
Neath did manage two late consolation tries, both converted by flyhalf Darren Morris, who had earlier missed a conversion and three penalties.

English champions Bath displayed the attacking potential which is likely to unsettle all their pool A opponents, scoring seven converted tries with two from England's Jeremy Guscott in a 55-26 thrashing of Edinburgh. Goalkicker Jon Callard finished with 25 points.

Bath led 38-9 at half-time and could have won by more. "There was some outstanding rugby in the first-half and the guys eased off the gas after the interval. Otherwise, it could have been another 70 or 80 points," said manager Jon Hall.
The only worry for the home side was the loss of dazzling rugby league recruit, Henry Paul, who was taken to hospital for X-rays after suffering a shoulder injury in the second-half.
Italy's two representatives, Treviso and Milan, both made disappointing starts in Ireland and Wales respectively.
Milan went down 23-5 to Munster in wet and windy conditions in Cork, failing to make much headway against the home forwards despite having a host of internationals in their own pack.
Left wing Brian Begley scored 20 of his side's points, with full-back Frederico Williams scoring Milan's solitary try.
"Given the reputation of Milan, who fielded an all-international side, I think we have every reason to be satisfied," said Munster coach Jerry Holland.
Treviso led 16-15 at half-time, but were kicked to defeat by Welsh fly-half Neil Jenkins who scored 23 points in Pontypridd's 28-22 pool A victory, taking him past 2,000 career points.

English referee Steve Lander awarded more than 20 penalties against Treviso, but Francesco Mazzariol matched Jenkins' 100 per cent success rate by landing five penalties and a conversion of his own first-half try.
Between them, Jenkins and Mazzariol had 14 shots of goal and kicked the lot. Poor discipline resulted in yellow cards for Italian centre Ivan Francescato and midfield colleague Pier Donati.
